title: cross-team-engineering-pulse-2028-07-19
content:
Cross-team engineering pulse — weekly leadership notes
Date: 2028-07-19
Facilitator / note owner: Maya Chen
Attendees: Maya Chen, Arjun Patel, Lena Ortiz, Noah Kim, Priya Desai, Elena Varga (observability), Marco Ruiz (platform), Samir Shah (SRE)

Purpose: quick alignment across serving-runtime, platform, observability, SRE and solutions engineering on production health, capacity planning, rollouts, and outstanding cross-team risks. Keep this lightweight — capture decisions and clear owners.

1) Quick metrics snapshot (top-level signals) — Lena
- 99th p95/p99 latency: steady for baseline endpoints; a 10–12% regression in p95 for short-chat routes in eu-west-1 during the Tues window (14:10–15:30 UTC).
- Error rate: increased 0.3% (client 5xx) correlated with caching layer misses during the same window.
- Cost per 1k tokens (hosted): slight uptick due to increased short-tail single-request traffic; Dedicated usage steady.
- Token throughput: demo customers ramping a 15% peak on weekdays; Dedicated pools have headroom ~22% before needing burst capacity.

Notes: we observed single-point kernel fallback on a small subset of nodes that increased CPU overhead (see RI-2287).

2) Incident follow-ups / ongoing RCA work — Samir / Noah
- Root cause hypothesis: kernel selection logic defaulted to an older BV kernel when sequence length < 64 on a recently rolled OS image; combined with a higher-than-expected eviction churn in KV cache.
- Action: create a short hotfix to pin kernel selection to v3.9 for short-chat model variants for the next 48h while we validate the long-lived fix (owner: Noah, jira/RI-2331). ETA: 2028-07-20 EOD for hotfix staged rollout.
- Observability ask: Elena to add a synthetic that hits short-chat route with seq_len=32 to catch future regressions (owner: Elena, done by 2028-07-21).

3) Rollouts / canaries update — Arjun
- Quantized Mistral-7B vq2 rollout: canary ran across 5% of traffic for 3 days. Quality metrics stable but p95 latency +8% on small requests.
- Decision: pause further rollout pending kernel selection hotfix; resume after 2 consecutive days of synthetic green. (Decision owner: Arjun)
- GH PR 5127 contains the batching/collar tuning — needs one more review from platform infra (Marco). Request: Marco to prioritize review in next 24h.

4) Dedicated capacity / capacity planning — Marco
- Forecast: two enterprise customers are scheduled to ramp in Q3; expected steady state increase ~45% non-burst. We have reserved GPU budget but need autoscaling policy tweaks.
- Proposal: add a mid-tier burst pool to cover 30% short spikes (cost vs SLA tradeoff). Request engineering sign-off on policy change and SRE to own throttling fallback.
- Action: Marco to send policy PR and cost estimate (owner: Marco, due 2028-07-22).

5) Private deployment checklist and customer onboarding blockers — Priya
- Two customers in final acceptance testing reported noisy neighbor delays when private control-plane config included shared NFS mount. Workaround: isolate model caches per tenant or switch to per-tenant local mount.
- Engineering ask: platform-eng to add per-tenant cache isolation option to private-deploy helm chart (owner: Priya + Marco, jira/RI-2402).

6) Observability / tracing gaps — Elena
- Traces currently drop KV cache tags on sampling; makes root-cause noisy. Proposal: add lightweight KV-cache-span flag for low-overhead tracing across short requests.
- Prioritization: medium. Elena to prototype and deliver a sampling tweak RFC by 2028-07-28.

7) Feature / experiments notes — Maya
- Auto-prefix caching experiment (A/B) shows 22% cost reduction on a small prompt-heavy corpus but increases cold-start latency for rare prompts. We will run an extended 2-week A/B with conservative TTLs. Owner: Maya, A/B start 2028-07-21.

8) Hiring / resourcing flags — Lena
- Hiring pipeline: 1 infra SWE offer accepted; remaining backend openings: 3 (runtime), 2 (platform) — expect hires Q3. Interim risk: slower velocity on platform PR reviews.

9) Risks & decisions needing leadership attention
- Risk: If kernel hotfix takes >72h to stabilize, we may need to roll back last week's node image to avoid customer impact (Decision: pre-authorize rollback; owner: Eng leads).
- Decision required: approve mid-tier burst pool (Marco) — action for execs to sign off by 2028-07-22 if cost acceptable.

10) Action items (clear owners + due dates)
- Noah: implement kernel pin hotfix and rollout plan (jira/RI-2331). Due 2028-07-20.
- Elena: add synthetic short-chat seq32 test and prototype KV-cache-span sampling flag. Synthetics by 2028-07-21; RFC prototype by 2028-07-28.
- Marco: submit autoscaling policy PR for mid-tier burst pool + cost estimate. Due 2028-07-22.
- Arjun: hold on quantized Mistral-7B rollout; coordinate resume after 2 green synthetic runs. Ongoing.
- Priya + Marco: add per-tenant cache isolation option to private-deploy helm chart (jira/RI-2402). Initial PR by 2028-07-26.
- Maya: start extended auto-prefix A/B on 2028-07-21 and monitor quality regressions daily.
- Samir: run canary stress test for eviction churn scenarios and publish results (jira/RI-2287). Due 2028-07-25.

11) Parking lot / unresolved questions
- We still need quant metrics on how much prefix caching interacts with token-level billing rounding for some customers — finance to weigh in. (Action: Maya to loop in finance).
- SLA language for burst pool needs legal review for Dedicated contracts. (Action: Marco to open legal consult ticket).

12) Quick wins / follow-ups for next week
- Prioritize synthetic for short-chat route (Elena).
- Marco to post cost tradeoffs doc for burst pool in #runtime-ops.
- Platform to add a short PR template checklist item: "does this change affect kernel selection?"

Meeting cadence: continue weekly leadership pulse, reduce to bi-weekly once kernel hotfix + burst pool decision are resolved.

Next meeting: 2028-07-26 09:30 PT

Notes & references: tickets called out above. If you want a focused readout for your execs, I can extract a 1-page status with decisions.

---
Notes to self (informal):
- follow up with Marco on whether burst pool can be region-scoped (EU-only) to reduce cost.
- check with solutions-eng about customers most sensitive to p95 (they usually call support first).
- leave room to revert Mistral quantization if kernel pin isn't safe.
